tasks.title: Setup Project Repository
tasks.description: Initialize a new Git repository for the project, including README, .gitignore, basic project structure, and UV project initialization.
tasks.details: Create a new repository on GitHub/GitLab. Add initial files: README.md, .gitignore (Python, Node, React), and a basic project structure (backend, frontend, docs). Initialize the Python backend using UV: run `uv init` in the backend directory to set up UV project files. UV will create the necessary structure including pyproject.toml, .python-version, README.md, and main.py. Ensure the .gitignore file includes entries for Python virtual environments. Document the project structure in the README, including instructions for using UV commands like `uv run` and `uv sync`. If migrating from an existing Python project, use `uv pip install -e .` to install dependencies from pyproject.toml. Set the appropriate Python version in the .python-version file (3.9 or higher) to ensure compatibility.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify repository is accessible, files are present, and structure matches project requirements. Confirm that UV initialization files (pyproject.toml, .python-version, main.py) exist in the backend directory. Test that running `uv run main.py` works without errors. Verify that the Python version specified in .python-version is installed and being used correctly. Ensure the project structure follows the architecture document specifications and that all necessary dependencies can be installed using `uv sync`.

tasks.title: Design and Implement Dashboard UI
tasks.description: Develop the Request Tracking Dashboard as specified in PRD section 4.2.1, focusing on status tracking, reporting, and interactive data visualization for workflow requests.
tasks.details:
Implement a React-based Request Tracking Dashboard per PRD section 4.2.1. The dashboard should provide:

- Request Status Overview: Display current status distribution of all tracked requests using interactive charts (bar, pie, line).
- Request Timeline Visualization: Visualize the lifecycle and progression of requests over time.
- Pending Actions Widget: Highlight outstanding actions for users.
- Recent Activity Feed: Show the latest updates and changes to requests.
- Performance Metrics Charts: Present key metrics such as average processing time, volume by status, and bottleneck identification.
- Search and Filter Interface: Enable advanced filtering by request type, status, date range, and assignee.

**Technical Requirements:**
- Use React for component-based architecture and state management[2][1].
- Leverage Tailwind CSS for styling and responsive design[3][4].
- Integrate high-performance, reusable dashboard components for charts, tables, and widgets[3][5].
- Optimize for large data sets with lazy loading, pagination, and data caching strategies.
- Ensure real-time updates for request status changes and activity feeds.
- Provide drill-down capability from summary views to detailed request information.
- Support export functionality for reports and data.
- Implement role-based access and authentication for dashboard features.
- Ensure accessibility (WCAG compliance) and mobile responsiveness.

**Integration Points:**
- Connect to backend API endpoints for request and metrics data.
- Integrate with notification system for alerts and pending actions.
- Link to detailed form views for each request type.

**Design Reference:**
- Follow best practices for dashboard layout, visual hierarchy, and usability as outlined in PRD 4.2.1 and modern React dashboard guides[2][3][5].
- Use consistent color coding for status indicators and clear navigation between dashboard sections.
tasks.testStrategy: Test that the Request Tracking Dashboard renders all widgets and charts correctly, updates in real time on status changes, and displays accurate metrics. Validate performance with large data sets using simulated API responses. Verify advanced filtering, search, and export features. Test responsive design across device sizes and accessibility compliance. Confirm integration with backend APIs and notification system. Ensure role-based access controls restrict features appropriately.

tasks.title: Design and Implement Digital Forms
tasks.description: Develop individual digital forms for each workflow described in PRD section 4.1, ensuring that every form matches the exact requirements and naming from the PRD. The forms must comprehensively cover the entire credit workflow process, including all submission, review, approval, modification, and configuration steps as specified.
tasks.details: For each form explicitly listed in PRD section 4.1, create a dedicated React form component with fields, validation, and workflow logic matching the PRD. Implement form submission, review, and approval flows as separate forms where required, using the exact form names and purposes from the PRD. Integrate each form with backend APIs. Ensure role-based field visibility and access per form, according to workflow requirements. Use controlled components for forms requiring real-time validation, complex state management, or dynamic field logic, and consider uncontrolled components for simple, static forms to optimize performance. Display errors clearly next to relevant fields and ensure all forms are accessible. Leverage libraries like React Hook Form or Formik for complex validation and state management where appropriate. All forms must be traceable to a specific PRD 4.1 requirement. Consider using modern React form practices including useState for simple forms and React Hook Form for more complex implementations to ensure optimal performance and maintainability.
tasks.testStrategy: Test each form for correct submission, validation, and role-based field visibility. Verify that each workflow and form from PRD section 4.1 is covered by a dedicated React form component, with API integration functioning as expected. Test form performance under various conditions, comparing controlled and uncontrolled implementations where applicable. Ensure accessibility standards are met and user feedback for errors is clear and helpful. Validate that all credit workflow processes are properly implemented according to the PRD specifications, and that every PRD 4.1 form is present and functional. Include tests for form submission handling, including proper preventDefault() implementation and validation before submission.
